text:
maria: Quick sync — I pushed the replay+multi-region drain benchmarks from last night to the artifacts bucket. Need eyes on methodology and the kernel-selection/regression bits.
ajay: link? also what's the headline: did we observe regressions or just expected tradeoffs?
maria: artifacts: gs://redwood-perf/replays/2026-03-15/drain-run-1.tar.gz
zheng: tl;dr: no catastrophic regressed qps, but P95 in fallback region increased ~12ms when we forced fallback to smaller-quant model.
sam: can you paste the command you ran so I can reproduce locally?
maria: sure: 
```
./replay-harness --model=rw-8b --kernels="auto,fast-attn" --batching=adaptive --qps=250 --regions=us-west-2,eu-west-1 --kv-cache=on --replay=synthetic+primed-replays --seed=42
```
elena: what do you mean by "synthetic+primed-replays"? we normally run either pure synthetic or exact replay. mixing sounds risky for apples-to-apples. :thinking:
maria: good call — methodology notes: we did 3 phases: (A) pure synthetic (client-shaped interarrival), (B) recorded replay (real request traces, no KV priming), (C) replay with KV priming enabled to measure cache warmup + drain scenarios. We compared A vs C to quantify prefix caching benefits and fallback delta.
ajay: how did you ensure kernel selection stayed consistent across regions? different GPUs might pick different kernels for same model -> kills apples-to-apples.
zheng: we pinned kernel selection via the runtime flag --kernel-lock=experimental:fast-attn for the controlled runs. For the automatic runs we captured chosen kernel per pod in the trace.
maria: exact command for kernel-locked run: 
```
./replay-harness --model=rw-8b --kernel-lock=fast-attn --gpu-profile=ampere-a10x --...other flags
```
benchy-bot: SUMMARY: run=1823456789-d1 | phase=C (replay+kv) | regions=us-west-2,eu-west-1 | qps=250 | p50/p95/p99(us-west) = 24ms/68ms/210ms | p50/p95/p99(eu-west) = 29ms/85ms/230ms | fallback-overhead=12ms | dropped=0.4%
sam: those p99s look high. Did the tail correlate with batch-size spikes?
zheng: yes — profiler shows intermittent large batches when region drain triggered cross-region routing. Kernel A has bad tail at sequence>512 due to kernel fallback path.
elena: can you share flamegraph link?
maria: flamegraphs: gs://redwood-perf/flame/1823456789/ — main hotspot is kv-cache-lookup lock and kernel-codepath (switch -> slower attention).
ajay: any perf regressions compared to last week's baseline?
benchy-bot: BASELINE (1822800000): p95(us-west)=60ms, p95(eu-west)=78ms. Delta: +8ms(us-west), +7ms(eu-west) in this run.
maria: regression mostly from enabling the new batching heuristic (adaptive->aggressive-prefetch). It reduced avg latency but increased tail when routing spikes occur.
sam: hypothesis: prefetch increases KV cache contention during drain because more concurrent lookups for similar prefixes. Do we have KV hotkey skew numbers?
zheng: yes: key-skew(top-100) went from 32%->46% after prefetch. I attached the small CSV to the artifact.
elena: action items?
ajay: 1) run kernel-locked apples-to-apples across both regions with same GPU type + same batcher config 2) reproduce with and without aggressive-prefetch 3) if prefetch is culprit, add small-leaky-bucket per-key to KV lookups 4) measure impact on tokens/sec and latency tail
maria: adding: instrument routing path to emit tag when fallback model used (we currently only log capacity reasons). that'll help correlate fallback->tail.
infra-bot: created ticket PERF-1423: "drain-run: correlate fallback model usage with tail latency" assigned to @maria.
benchy-bot: quick note: when forcing fallback model (rw-3b) we saw model-switch overhead ~11-13ms across regions; KV priming reduced that to ~4-5ms after warmup.
sam: for the apples-to-apples kernel tests, can we use the harness flag --force-gpu=ampere-a10x on both regions in CI?
maria: yes, will schedule a locked run tonight with that exact config and attach raw traces.
ajay: please include the exact git sha of runtime + kernel patches in the artifacts. we had subtle behavior changes last time.
maria: good reminder — added: runtime sha: 9f3b2a7, kernel shim: b7d8fa1.
zheng: small experiment idea: change batching heuristic to prefer small fixed max_batch for the first 200ms after a failover event. Should reduce tail when drain/routing happens. can try A/B in Canary.
elena: SGTM. also add an eval prompt set to detect quality regressions from fallback model to ensure UQ doesn't regress while optimizing for latency.
sam: last ask — can we get raw packet-level interarrival stats for the replay? I want to verify client-side jitter isn't being emulated poorly.
maria: yes, will upload pcap + interarrival hist to same bucket.
ajay: thanks — let's reconvene after the kernel-locked run and the prefetch-off run. If tail persists, prioritize the per-key leaky bucket and limiting prefetch concurrency.
maria: thanks team — I'll post results here when the locked run completes. :rocket:
